subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Get out of hand
solution:
The correct answer is '**Go out of control**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Get out of hand**" refers to a situation becoming difficult to control or manage. (नियंत्रण से बाहर हो जाना)

 
 
• **Example**: The party **got out of hand** when too many uninvited guests showed up, causing chaos.
 
 
 
• **Go out of control** is synonymous with "**get out of hand**" and describes a situation or behaviour that cannot be controlled or managed anymore. (नियंत्रण से बाहर हो जाना)
 
 
• **Example**: Without proper project management, the software development timeline **got out of control**.
 
 
 
• "**Get out of hand**" directly aligns with situations that escalate beyond control, accurately depicted by "**Go out of control**."
 
• Hence, the correct meaning is **Go out of control**.

Therefore, the correct answer is "**Option 2**".

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keep control of hand** is not a recognized idiom and does not relate directly to "get out of hand."
 
• **Hands should be crossed** is also not relevant to the meaning of "get out of hand" and doesn't convey a similar message.
 
• **Fall from hand** doesn't capture the essence of losing control or management over a situation.
